title: Silence snapped up for $1.3 billion - Nature Biotechnology
text:
German pharma Merck KGaA is buying UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal worth $1.3 billion. Through the acquisition, Merck gains access to divesiran, a short interfering RNA (siRNA) that is set for phase 3 trials for the rare blood cancer polycythemia vera. In people with this condition, the bone marrow produces too many red blood cells, which increases the risk of cardiovascular and thrombotic events.Divesiran targets the liver, where it works by finding and destroying the mRNA for the transmembrane protease serine 6 (TMPRSS6) gene. TMPRSS6 acts as a negative regulator of hepcidin, a natural hormone that regulates iron. Lowering TMPRSS6 protein production results in higher hepcidin, which reduces the amount of iron in circulation and available in the bone marrow. With less iron available, red blood production slows.
